A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Intelligent Go-Explore and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. All 26 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on Game of 24, BabyAI, and TextWorld, including component ablations, archive-size measurements, and prompt-robustness experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C, including success rates and uncertainty estimates.

M1.justification: The state-selection, action-selection, archive-filtering, and action-history procedures are unchanged, as are Algorithm 1 and the prompts. Rewording in Appendix D does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, five BabyAI task families with text and visual observations, and three TextWorld games. v4 removes brief TextWorld task descriptions from Section 4.3, but their detailed descriptions remain in Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Figures 2–4 and Tables 2–5, including DFS/BFS, random actions, naive LLM, ReAct, Reflexion, GLAM, and classic Go-Explore in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, environment configurations, action budgets, model variants, and prompting protocols remain unchanged. Table 4 already measured archive size in v3; correcting its caption does not establish a changed metric.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same component ablations, foundation-model comparisons, archive-size analysis, and prompt-robustness experiments. The example Cooking Game trajectory in Appendix B.3 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Reported seed counts, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, 10,000 bootstrap resamples, and chi-square tests are unchanged. The Table 4 caption correction removes an incorrect metric description without changing uncertainty estimates or reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Game of 24 success remains 100% and TextWorld Coin Collector success remains 88%; Tables 2–5 retain their values.

T1.justification: The simulator-reset assumption, mathematical formulation, and Game of 24 search-space bound remain unchanged. Neither version adds or removes a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: foundation-model guidance throughout Go-Explore, improved exploration across modalities, and advantages over the reported baselines.

C2.justification: Explanations of exploration behavior, archive filtering, baseline failures, scalability, stochastic-environment extensions, and foundation-model biases are retained. Appendix D.2 and D.4 wording changes restate existing mechanisms and limitations.

D1.justification: Environment specifications, prompts, response parsing, fallback behavior, hyperparameters, model identifiers, API costs, and code-access information are unchanged. Removing the short main-text task summaries does not remove the detailed appendix documentation.

R1.justification: v4 removes the Treasure Hunter citation to Parisotto and Salakhutdinov (2018) and its Neural Map bibliography entry. The substantive research positioning in Section 6 and Appendix F is unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the TextWorld introduction, lightly edits Sections 3 and 4.3 and Appendix D, and removes duplicated wording in the acknowledgments. It adds the ICLR 2025 publication header while retaining the section and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v4 adds publication headers, adjusts text flow and Table 3 placement, and corrects Table 4's caption by removing 'for the success rate.' Figures and table structures are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves clarity by correcting Table 4's misleading success-rate caption and polishing several passages. Removing the short TextWorld descriptions reduces immediate main-text context, but Appendix B.3 preserves the details. The methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
